I found and recorded a contradiction synthesis about whether pure imitation learning is enough for driving. 

The synthesis (ID 44d8aea6-14b3-566c-9a9d-70ec8c6cd7d9) highlights that:

- One set of papers (claim IDs 09081b52-e1ad-5843-9bbc-8565cf5aea59 and 639f88c8-001d-587a-bae9-390fb3c89dcf) concludes pure imitation learning has limitations and is insufficient even with large datasets and mid-level input/output representations.
- Another paper (claim ID 443f6210-6468-59f8-8167-b719d39fc8fd) demonstrates that an end-to-end trained neural network via imitation learning (ALVINN) can successfully steer a car on public roads.

This creates a clear contradiction regarding the sufficiency of pure imitation learning for driving.
